MISSING GUARANTEE: the resulting buffer carries no NUL terminator and no check ensures one exists in-bounds, so the C-string invariant is violated. UNSAFE USE: the unterminated buffer is handed to C-string parsers (sscanf) that scan until NUL, reading past the end of the allocation. CONSEQUENCE: out-of-bounds heap read (KASAN slab-OOB, info leak / crash). Transferable pattern: usercopy of attacker-sized length into an exactly-sized allocation, followed by any string-consuming API (sscanf, simple_strtoul/strtol, strlen, strcmp, strchr, strcpy/strscpy-from-unterminated) without memdup_user_nul, strndup_user, or an explicit terminator slot. Search guidance: grep call sites of memdup_user followed by string parsers; kmalloc/copy_from_user with exact user length then string ops; copy helpers lacking a terminator byte; and verify the fix primitive (memdup_user_nul / strndup_user / len+1 allocation). BRANCHES: branch1=debugfs-write-memdup-sscanf - debugfs (and analogous debug-control) write file_operations handlers across drivers that memdup_user or kmalloc+copy_from_user an attacker-sized buffer and pass it to sscanf/simple_strtoul-style parsers without NUL termination; branch2=sysfs-store-attr-terminator - sysfs ->store() attribute callbacks (device/driver/bus/class/module attrs) that copy_from_user into exact- or fixed-size buffers and then use string parsers or strcmp/strlen/strchr on possibly-unterminated data; branch3=proc-config-write-unterminated - /proc, configfs, and other textual control-file write handlers that copy user data of attacker-chosen length and consume it with string functions assuming termination; branch4=ioctl-sock-usercopy-string - ioctl, setsockopt/getsockopt, netlink, and char-device fops paths that copy_from_user into variable-length buffers and then use string helpers (sscanf, strtoul, strcmp, strchr, strscpy) on the unterminated result.'

        i = src.find('{', m.start())
